messages.subject: mlg.filter
parts:
Hello evryone!

Can I please know whether mlg.filter is a way of correcting clonal bias or do we still need to clone-correct? I thought it is a way of clone-correcting but the part on clone-correction in https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/poppr/vignettes/mlg.html#clone-correction confused me.

"Notice how we are getting different results based on the order of samples. This does not mean that the procedure doesn’t work, it just means that we must be careful when clone-correcting modified multilocus genotypes"

I understand that mlg.filter collapses mlgs into clonal lineages based on genetic distances but does it get rid of the clones as well? 


Also how do you propose to do the linkage disequlibrium analysis and AMOVA and other structure analysis using contracted genotypes?


Earlier, people used to publish results original and clone corrected data for comparison. 
How should I report results with filtered mlgs? Do I report it with original data or do I report it after clone correction of the filtered mlg data?

Thank you!

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] mlg.filter
parts: I understand that mlg.filter collapses mlgs into clonal lineages based on genetic distances but does it get rid of the clones as well?
No. It does not remove clones, it provides multilocus lineage assignment for each sample. You must use clone-correction if you want to have one representative sample per multilocus lineage.
Also how do you propose to do the linkage disequlibrium analysis and AMOVA and other structure analysis using contracted genotypes?

The AMOVA function in poppr already has a method of performing analysis on filtered data. The only drawback is that you are then unable to assess error from within-individual variance if you don't have haploids. https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/poppr.amova.html

If you have an analysis that uses a distance matrix, you can obtain that from the mlg.filter() function by setting stats = "DISTANCES" (https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/mlg.filter.html). This will give you a distance matrix for the collapsed multilocus lineages.

For other analyses, you may want to run clone-correction on shuffled data sets to get a sense of the variability. I would caution against using clone-correction for linkage analyses unless you have a large sample size after clone-correction as these are known to result in non-significant values of linkage (https://zkamvar.github.io/dissertation/5-factors-influencing-inference-of-clonality-in-diploid-populations.html#fig:sim4).

Earlier, people used to publish results original and clone corrected data for comparison. 
How should I report results with filtered mlgs? Do I report it with original data or do I report it after clone correction of the filtered mlg data?

I would recommend to be as transparent as possible. Be sure to report the distance metric, threshold, and algorithm used to define the MLLs. The multilocus lineages are most useful for reporting genotypic diversity statistics such as those produced by the poppr() function. 

Hope that helps,
Zhian
